title: Work
text:
ONGOING PROJECTS:

M.A. Thesis, Harvard University 2026 Proposed to write a thesis on the history of Hepatitis B in modern China and discuss the stigmatization of the disease.

FINISHED PROJECTS:

Undergraduate Honors Thesis, Tsinghua University 2024 Advisor: Prof. Yubin Shen, Dept. of History of Science Title: “From Far Eastern Association Of Tropical Medicine: Racial Concepts in Medical Research in Tropical Colonies in Asia” Research and analysis of FEATM from 1908-1938, with focus on racial concepts and power dynamics
Research Assistant, Tsinghua University 2022 Advisor: Prof. Zheran Wang, Dept. of History of Science Studied the restoration of the aircraft from Da Vinci’s manuscripts and sketches and planned the “Reaching the Clouds – Leonardo Da Vinci’s Flight and Construction Machinery Exhibition” at the Science Museum of Tsinghua University

CONFERENCE TALKS AND TAUGHT WORKSHOPS

Conference Talk, “The Similarities and Differences between The Kauṭilīya Arthaśāstra and Master Lyu’s Spring and Autumn Annals,” The Intersection of Art and Technology: 2023 Forum for Young Scholars in Indian Studies, Beijing, October 2023.
Workshop, “Quarantine treatment and epidemic prevention systems: A cultural perspective in modern China,” Faculty of Humanities Modern Chinese History Workshop, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, 28 June 2023.

title: About
text: Maggie Liang is currently an M.A. student in the RSEA program at Harvard. She received her B.A. from Tsinghua University, majoring in Philosophy and minoring in History of Science. Her research interest is history of medicine in China, particularly in traditional medicine and issues related to hepatitis B in modern Asia. She loves dancing and cooking during her spare time.
